_comment: Config for wp_screenshot.py — the VISUAL-EVIDENCE capture: a rendered full-page PNG of a live page, hashed and timestamped so a screenshot can be cited in a report the same way a DOM capture is. Analyst-tunable without editing Python. RULE 1: never put a case value here. RULE 3: the code holds the capture logic, this file holds the knobs the code reads.

capture._comment: How the page is rendered. timeout_seconds bounds the Playwright navigation (raise it for a slow or challenge-walled target). The browser User-Agent sent to the target is the shared Android default (wp_ua <- fetch_profile.json -> ua_pool; project decision: Android, not desktop). Add a `user_agent` key here only to override it — for example to match the client a campaign expects, so the page renders the way a victim would see it.

layout._comment: Where evidence screenshots and their manifest are written under a case: cases/<case>/evidence/<dir>/<host>/<UTC-timestamp>.png, with one manifest per case listing every capture (url, final_url, captured_at, sha256, pixel dimensions, page title). Captures are timestamped and never overwritten, so two captures of the same page date any change between them.

collection._comment: AUTOMATIC per-host screenshot during /cti collection (collect_core.collect_host -> tools/collect_screenshot.py -> wp_screenshot). `enabled` is the default when env HARNESS_SCREENSHOT is unset (HARNESS_SCREENSHOT=0 turns it off, =1 on); it costs no credits, so review and auto mode both take it. Every host collected live, or recovered from a Wayback capture, gets one full-page PNG in the same custody-tracked store as capture_screenshot (cases/<case>/evidence/screenshots/<host>/<UTC>.png: sha256, custody line, seal, seal_status). A hostile host is shot only through the pool exit its fetch used, never direct; an archive-only host is shot at its Wayback URL. `per_host_timeout_seconds` bounds one host's shot (browser launch + navigation + verify) and is still clamped to the active phase deadline; a timeout or any failure is recorded as `screenshot: failed (<reason>)` and never fails the collection.
